newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine group to protest anti-Jewish attacks.
newsitem.headline: Argentine group to protest anti-Jewish attacks.

text.p: Argentina's best-known human rights group, the Mothers of the Plaza de Mayo, on Wednesday called for a demonstration outside the presidential palace to protest anti-Semitic attacks.

The group, best known for its struggle to punish military human rights abusers, said it was outraged by the failure of investigators to find those responsible for a string of incidents including two bloody bomb attacks. Unknown vandals desecrated a Jewish cemetery over the weekend and a bomb threat was made against a Jewish hospital early on Wednesday.

"Faced with the impunity of the previous attacks, and the permanent attacks suffered by the Jewish community, such as the recent violation of the tombs in the La Tablada cemetery and the bomb threat against the Israelite Hospital, the Mothers of the Plaza de Mayo call (a demonstration)," it said.
The demonstration would be held on Thursday, it said.

Police bomb experts searched a big Buenos Aires Jewish hospital early on Wednesday after it received a bomb threat, but found nothing. The anonymous caller claimed to represent a group called the "National Dignity Commandos," which he said was responsible for the desecration of the cemetery, but Jewish groups said they had no record of such a group.

Unidentified vandals broke into Argentina's main Jewish cemetery just outside Buenos Aires late on Saturday, smashing tombstones, spraying them with swastikas and daubing the place with graffiti calling the Holocaust a "great Jewish lie."

Amid the continuing anti-Semitic incidents, an appeals court upheld on Wednesday charges against four police officers linked to the July 1994 car bombing of the AMIA centre in Buenos Aires that killed 86 people and injured hundreds more.

Argentina's police and courts have been criticised by Israel, the United States and Jewish groups for failing to completely solve the AMIA bombing and a 1992 bomb attack on the Israeli embassy in Buenos Aires, which killed 29 people. The Americans and Israelis say they suspect Iran was behind the bomb attacks.
